name: Question 2
problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=1,{x}_{2}=2,{x}_{3}=-4$ and ${x}_{4}=4$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$
worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=1,{x}_{2}=2,$ ${x}_{3}=-4,$ and ${x}_{4}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-1)(x-2)(x-(-4))(x-4) \\  & =(x-1)(x-2)(x+4)(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)(x-2)(x+4)(x-4) & =({x}^{2}-3x+2)({x}^{2}-16) \\  & ={x}^{4}-16{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3}+48x+2{x}^{2}-32 \\  & ={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-14{x}^{2}+48x-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-14{x}^{2}+48x-32.$

Question 2

The quartic polynomial P(x) has roots x1=1,x2=2,x3=−4 and x4=4 and the coefficient of the quartic term is 1. Find P(x).

a
x4+5x3−14x2+12x
b
x4−3x3−14x2+48x−32
c
x4−4x3+6x−32
d
x4−3x3−13x2+24x−32
e
x4−5x3−4x2+8x−32
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since our quartic polynomial has roots x1=1,x2=2, x3=−4, and x4=4, and the coefficient of the quartic term is a=1, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)(x−x4)=1(x−1)(x−2)(x−(−4))(x−4)=(x−1)(x−2)(x+4)(x−4)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

(x−1)(x−2)(x+4)(x−4)=(x2−3x+2)(x2−16)=x4−16x2−3x3+48x+2x2−32=x4−3x3−14x2+48x−32.

Therefore, P(x)=x4−3x3−14x2+48x−32.
